newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq increases food rations handed to its citizens.
newsitem.headline: Iraq increases food rations handed to its citizens.

text.p: Iraq said on Tuesday it was increasing heavily subsidised food rations in August made available under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
Rice and pulses and other essentials sold to Iraqis at give-away prices will be increased next month as more food bought under the pact has arrived in the country.
According to the Iraqi News Agency INA, each Iraqi will get 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) of rice instead of two kg (4.4 lb) and one kg (2.2 lb) of pulses instead of half a kg (1.1 lb).
Each Iraqi is also entitled to nine kg of wheat flour, two kg of sugar, 150 gram of tea, 250 gram of soap, 350 gram of detergents and 150 gram of table salt.

Iraq has been under stringent U.N. sanctions since its troops invaded Kuwait in 1990. But under its deal with the United Nations, Iraq was allowed from December to June to export $2 billion worth of oil to raise money to buy urgently needed goods.
The deal was renewed by the U.N. Security Council for another six months from June 8. But the exports have been held up pending U.N. approval of an Iraqi procurement and distribution plan.
A U.N. source in Baghdad told Reuters on Monday that nearly 1.1 million tonnes of food and medicine had reached the country under the first six months of the deal out of 2.2 million tonnes purchased.
Iraq has frequently complained about delays in the arrival of medical and food supplies, blaming the United States.
